_comment: PaperDrop configuration. Paths are user-scoped; ~ expands.
_comment_source: mode=manifest reads a JSON manifest (recommended: it carries a sha256, so an unchanged image is never re-downloaded). mode=image treats the URL as a plain always-updated image and has NO manifest consistency guarantee.
_comment_paths: Where the current and previous image are cached.
_comment_log: One rotating file: max_bytes per file, keep backups, so the rotating log is bounded by max_bytes * (keep + 1). The files macOS writes for the scheduled runs are capped at max_bytes each too, which keeps every log PaperDrop can write at about 5 MB in total (1 MB x 3 + 1 MB x 2).
_comment_http: max_bytes caps a single download; retries apply only to transient failures (timeouts, 429, 5xx).
_comment_apply: scaling=fill keeps the aspect ratio and fills the screen. helper_path is the compiled macOS helper (leave empty to auto-detect). xfce_image_style stays null to preserve whatever background style you configured in Xfce. confirm_attempts/confirm_delay_seconds control how long to wait for the desktop to report the new wallpaper: some desktops keep answering with the old one for a moment after the change.
_comment_schedule: Used by the installer to create the user-level schedule. catch_up_interval_minutes adds a periodic cheap check so a run missed while the machine was asleep happens soon after it wakes; the same-day check makes those runs nearly free. 0 disables it. catch_up_on_login adds a run at login (macOS RunAtLoad; systemd Persistent on Linux), and watch_screen_changes installs the resident macOS watcher that re-applies the image after a screen change or a wake. screen_poll_seconds is how often that watcher asks the desktop for every screen, because a display reconnected after a run can come back with the wallpaper it remembered without any event reaching us (0 turns the poll off). All of them are read at run time: change them and run "paperdrop install" again for the ones the installer uses.
